label: <DEL> step of long sequences starting with x/m/s/p/1/t
explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit: 80% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (t == L), the step where the model emits original token 0. Even so it fires on only about 10% of delimiter steps. Rate goes up with sequence length (L=9 holds 52% of mass, L>=8 about 80%) and depends strongly on the first token (the token being output): x, m, p, 1, s and t give about 4-5x lift, a, f, q and i are weaker. The next token, orig(1), also matters (s, m, x, i, d). The remaining ~20% of mass is on the last few original-phase steps of long sequences (to_go 6-8 counted at the DEL step; original-phase steps 7-8), usually just before <DEL>, and mostly on first occurrences of tokens. Almost never fires in the copy phase (17 steps) or at t<2. The largest activations (up to 0.256) are at <DEL> in L=8-9 sequences that start with x/m/s/t/1. Counting how many tokens from the preferred set appear did not do better than the first-token rule, so this looks like a graded, distributed code over token identity plus length rather than a clean boolean. Dev F1 is about 0.43.
